draft.title: Stomata
card: Stomata are tiny pores, mostly on the underside of leaves. Each pore sits between two guard cells, which change shape to open or close it.
When a stoma is open, carbon dioxide diffuses in for photosynthesis and oxygen diffuses out. Water vapour also diffuses out of the leaf.
A plant cannot have gas exchange without some water loss. Open stomata favour photosynthesis, and closed stomata save water.
Stomata tend to be open in bright light when water is plentiful. They tend to close when the plant is short of water, such as on a hot, dry day. This is how a vascular plant regulates its water.
draft.remember: Open stomata let carbon dioxide in and water out. Closing them saves water.

a.q: Which statement best explains why a plant cannot keep its stomata open all the time?
opts: Open stomata let water vapour escape from the leaf
Open stomata stop oxygen leaving the leaf
Open stomata block carbon dioxide from entering
Open stomata stop the guard cells changing shape
a.why: Water vapour diffuses out through open stomata, so a plant that stayed open would lose too much water. Oxygen leaves and carbon dioxide enters through open stomata, so the other options reverse what happens.
a.clue: Think about what else leaves the leaf when a pore is open.

b.q: On a hot, dry afternoon in Mildura, a grapevine is short of water. What is the most likely response of its stomata, and the effect on photosynthesis?
opts: They close, saving water but limiting carbon dioxide intake
They close, saving water and raising carbon dioxide intake
They open, saving water but limiting carbon dioxide intake
They open, gaining water and raising carbon dioxide intake
b.why: A plant short of water tends to close its stomata to cut water loss. With the pores closed, less carbon dioxide can enter, so photosynthesis is limited. Opening them would increase water loss, not save water.
b.clue: Closed pores block water vapour and carbon dioxide both.

a.best: Open stomata let water vapour escape from the leaf

b.best: They close, saving water but limiting carbon dioxide intake

problems.detail: Why (a) says the other options all 'reverse what happens', but 'Open stomata stop the guard cells changing shape' is not a reversal of anything on the card. Guard cells change shape to open and close the pore, so this option is simply false, not reversed.
